name: Tsotsil
catalog_quote: Descriptions of Z Tsotsil characterize prosodic prominence at two levels – the word and the phrase. At the word level, stress falls on the initial syllable of the root; at the phrase level, it falls on the final syllable of the ιP (Laughlin 1975,23; Haviland 1981,14) (stress being predictable, it is not marked in the orthography).

sources.quote: Laughlin 1975:23: "Primary stress occurs on the final syllable of single words in isolation except in affective verbs with -luh, first person plural exclusive suffixes, and reduplicated stems of two syllables.
